cme.note: CME first seen to the East in STEREO A COR2 beginning at 2026-08-14T05:09Z, as well as by GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. This CME was not visible in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 in real-time due to a data gap which began at 2026-08-14T04:48Z. The source of this event is a filament eruption centered at approx. S10E20 with liftoff beginning at approx. 2026-08-14T04:00Z. This filament is heavily deflected to the West as it erupts as seen in SDO AIA, STEREO A EUVI and GOES SUVI 304. Field line opening, dimming and post eruptive arcades are also visible in SDO AIA 171, 193, STEREO A EUVI 195 and GOES SUVI 284.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.

cme.note: CME first seen as a halo to the SE by STEREO A COR2 beginning at 2026-08-14T07:38Z, as well as by GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. This CME was not visible in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 in real-time due to a data gap which began at 2026-08-14T04:48Z. The source of this event is a C4.1 flare from Active Region 14503 (S17W57) seen peaking at 2026-08-14T07:01Z in SDO AIA 131. Field line opening, dimming and post eruptive arcades are also visible in SDO AIA 94, 171, 193, STEREO A EUVI 195 and GOES SUVI 284.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.

cme.note: CME observed to the W in STEREO A COR2 and as a NE partial halo in GOES CCOR-1, not seen in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 in real-time due to DSN gap, but imagery became available with later backfill. The source is far-sided, only likely visible as field line movement over the NE limb in SDO AIA 171 starting as early as 2026-08-14T10:42Z and over the NE limb in STEREO A EUVI 195 starting around 2026-08-14T10:55Z. This CME is preceded by a faint front that is quickly overtaken by the main bulk of this CME.

cmeAnalyses.note: UPDATED BULK measurement based on best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.
SHOCK measurement based on best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.
PRELIMINARY measurement based on triangulation between STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.

cme.note: CME first seen to the W in STEREO A COR2 starting at 2026-08-14T18:23Z. It is also seen to the W in GOES CCOR-1. In real time, this CME is covered by a data gap in SOHO LASCO C2/C3. The source of this CME is most likely related to moving field lines seen beyond the W limb in SDO AIA 171 beginning around 2026-08-14T17:18Z. An eruption that may be related can be seen in STEREO A EUVI 195 near former AR 14505 (located approximately N15W145) beginning around 2026-08-14T16:55Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit between GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2.

cme.note: CME first seen to the N in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2026-08-14T22:24Z. It is also seen to the N in SOHO LASCO C3 and to the NW in STEREO A COR2. The majority of the CME is obscured by the pylon in GOES CCOR-1. A possible source is a small filament eruption beyond the N limb best seen in GOES SUVI 304 starting at 2026-08-14T21:52Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

cme.note: This CME is visible to the NW in STEREO A COR2 imagery and to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2 imagery before a real-time data gap starting around 2026-08-15T04:24Z. This CME is not yet visible in SOHO LASCO C3 due to the aforementioned data gap. In GOES CCOR-1, there is an Earth-shine imaging artifact obscuring the initial view of the CME, but is likely seen to the NE following the imaging artifact. There is no clear source for this CME, but it is believed to be far sided. This CME follows in the same path of the CME first seen in SOHO LASCO C2 imagery starting at 2026-08-14T22:24Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters based on best fit using SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. There is a more narrow feature ahead of the front tracked in SOHO LASCO C2 which may adjust the associated longitude by +/- 10 degrees.

cme.note: CME first seen to the ENE in SOHO LASCO C2 starting around 2026-08-15T06:48Z. It is also seen to the ENE in SOHO LASCO C3, and GOES CCOR-1 and to the NE in STEREO A COR2. The source may be related to some fluctuation in filament structures seen near the E limb in SDO AIA 304 for several hours before and after the CME start time, but no clear filament liftoff can be seen.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit among SOHO LASCO C2, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. CME is very slow to start, so the triangulated measurement is based on later frames.

cme.note: CME first seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2 starting around 2026-08-15T07:24Z. It is also seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 and to the NNW in STEREO A COR2. There is no good source candidate on the Earth-facing disk, so the source is most likely far-sided. This is consistent with measurements.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit among SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2.

cme.note: CME first seen to the NNE in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2026-08-15T11:36Z. It is also seen to the NNE in SOHO LASCO C3 but is not seen in STEREO A COR2 and is mostly obscured by the pylon in GOES CCOR-1. There is no definitive source candidate on the Earth-facing disk, so the source is most likely far-sided. This feature partially overlaps with CME: 2026-08-15T07:24Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement chosen due to single perspective and lack of source candidate.

cme.note: CME first seen to the NNE in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2026-08-15T13:48Z. It is also seen to the NNE in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 and to the NNW in STEREO A COR2. There is no definitive source candidate on the Earth-facing disk, so the source is most likely far-sided. This is consistent with measurement.

cme.note: CME first seen to the W in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2026-08-16T20:03Z. It is also seen to the W in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 and to the NE in STEREO A COR2. The majority of this CME was missed in real time by SOHO LASCO C3 due to a data gap between downlinks. This CME is associated with a C8.2 class flare from AR 14506 (N10W42) that peaked at 2026-08-16T19:28Z. The flare is best seen in SDO AIA 131.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit among SOHO LASCO C2, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 as well as on visible source location.

cme.note: CME visible to the NW in GOES CCOR-1 and the NE in STEREO A COR2. The CME is not visible in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 in real-time due to a gap in the DSN. The source is likely an eruption from AR 14506 (approximately N12W51) or AR 14510 (approximately N13W64). The eruption from AR 14506 may be the most likely candidate, starting around 2026-08-17T04:52Z with dimming and post-eruptive arcades best seen in SDO AIA 193. The eruption is also seen in STEREO A EUV 195/304.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2 in SWPC_CAT.

cme.note: CME visible to the NE in GOES CCOR-1 and possibly faintly to the NE in STEREO A COR2 imagery. Not visible in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 in real-time due to a data gap starting at 2026-08-17T03:42Z. The source is not found in available EUV imagery, and is likely beyond the East limb from the point of view of SDO AIA imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane of sky measurement based on GOES CCOR-1 imagery in SWPC_CAT.

cme.note: This CME is visible to the northwest in GOES CCOR-1 imagery. This event is not visible in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 or STEREO A COR2 imagery in real-time. The source is likely related to a C2.0 flare from Active Region 14510 (N12W65) starting around 2026-08-17T17:00Z as seen in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304, GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304, and STEREO A EUVI 195/304 imagery. A subsequent opening of field lines is visible over the northeast limb in GOES SUVI 284 imagery at this time.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the on-disk source longitude.

cme.note: This CME is visible to the west in GOES CCOR-1 and SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery. This event is directed towards STEREO A and is therefore not observable in the STEREO A COR2 coronagraph. The source is likely an eruption from Active Region 14510 (N14W80) starting around 2026-08-18T13:30Z seen in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304, GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304, and STEREO A EUVI 195/304 imagery. An opening of field lines is visible over the northwest limb at this time in SDO AIA 193 and GOES SUVI 195/284 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the source longitude.

An opening of field lines is visible over the western limb at this time in GOES SUVI 195/284 and SDO AIA 193 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters based on best fit of features using the source location for lat/lon parameters.

cme.note: This CME is visible to the E in GOES CCOR-1 and to the NE in STEREO A COR2 imagery. There is  a real-time data gap for SOHO LASCO C2/C3 currently. This CME is associated with the M8.1 flare from Active Region 14513 (N05E80) peaking at 2026-08-20T11:42Z as seen in SDO/AIA 131, 193, 171, and 304. Associated moving/opening field lines are visible to the E/NE in SDO/AIA 193 and 171, as well as filament material in SDO/AIA 304. These features are additionally visible in GOES SUVI wavelengths.
